title: Understanding Friction at Atomic Level
theory:
**Big idea:** Even a "smooth" surface is a mountain range at the atomic scale. Friction comes from bonds forming and breaking at the few tiny points where the surfaces actually touch.

**Surfaces are rough up close:** a polished steel plate looks flat to the eye, but under a powerful microscope its surface is very irregular.

**The real area of contact is tiny**
When one body rests on another, they only truly touch at the tips of these bumps. The **real area of contact** is much smaller than the visible area.

**What happens at the contact points**
1. The particles of the two surfaces come very close, so **molecular forces** act across them.
2. **Molecular bonds** form at these contact points.
3. When one body is pulled, the bonds **break**, the material under them **deforms**, and new bonds form.
4. The deformation sends **vibrations** into the bodies.
5. The vibrations die out and their energy becomes **random motion of the particles**, so the bodies **heat up**.

So a force is needed to **start** the motion (to break the bonds) and to **keep it going** (bonds keep forming and breaking).

> 💡 This is why rubbing your hands together warms them up.

questions.prompt: Seen under a powerful microscope, a polished steel surface appears:
questions.explanation: Polished surfaces are very irregular at the atomic scale.

questions.prompt: When one body is kept on another, the real area of contact is:

options.text: Much smaller than the visible area of contact
Exactly equal to the visible area
Much larger than the visible area

questions.explanation: The surfaces touch only at the tips of the bumps.

questions.prompt: At the actual points of contact between two surfaces:

options.text: Molecular bonds form between the particles of the two surfaces

questions.explanation: The particles get close enough to bond.

questions.prompt: Bodies get heated when they are rubbed against each other because:

options.text: Vibrations from breaking bonds and deformation end up as random motion of particles

questions.explanation: The vibration energy spreads out as random motion of the particles, which we feel as heat.

options.text: An electromagnetic effect between particles at the surfaces
A purely mechanical effect with no atomic cause

questions.explanation: The bonds at the contact points are electromagnetic.
